clock: the computer that ran the builder (UK time on Richard's PC)

rule.bands: A above 90%; B+ above 82.5% to 90%; B above 75% to 82.5%; C+ above 66.67% to 75%; C above 58.33% to 66.67%; C- above 50% to 58.33%; D above 25% to 50%; F up to 25%
rule.rank: percentile rank = (scores below + half the ties) / population size; the population of an item is every stock holding a score on that item from its registered run (or its published memo)
rule.registered_run: the newest live card in the conveyor's trays whose run holds scores; dry, cancelled and control runs never enter
rule.boundaries: per item, the lowest score that earned each grade today; null where no score earned that grade
rule.comparison_set: the stocks analysed by the new approach (the Sets of Questions/Items approach)
rule.fixed_letters: on memo topics 5, 6, 8, 11 and 12 a cell carrying fixed_letter shows the Rater's own letter from a real-world measure (A to F, no sub-grade), never re-cut; its rank and p are information only (D-SQ-267, D-SQ-271)
rule.fixed_cutoffs: v1.5 (his Messages 427 and 428; D-SQ-280): three letter rules, one per item, stated in each item's letter_rule. RANK within the population of stocks scored on the same scale (A top 10%; B next 15%, B+ its top half; C next 25% in thirds C+, C, C-; D next 25%; F bottom 25%) for the judgement items. His FIXED CUT-OFFS on the number (A 90 and above; B+ 82.5 to 89; B 75 to 82.4; C+ 66.67 to 74; C 58.33 to 66.66; C- 50 to 58.32; D 25 to 49; F below 25) for the items where 50 means neither positive nor negative: topics 1 and 2, Thesis's Change Forces' Strength, the External change forces and Internal change forces group judgements and their questions. The Rater's letter from his cut-offs on the MEASURE for topics 6, 8, 11 and 12, the number placed inside the letter's band. Rank and the percentile stay on every cell for information.
rule.scales: v1.5: every cell carries scale_tag; a rank letter is cut only among cells of the same scale (rater-v3 = the Rater v3.0 after the memo; rater-v2 and rater-v1-keyed = earlier Raters; writer-1.9 = the Investment Analyst's own score as it wrote the answer, the old method; writer-memo = the memo Analyst's own topic score). Old-method cells are labelled and stay until the Rater scores that stock's memo.
rule.scale_caveat: scores tagged rater-v1-keyed were set by the Rater of 1-Nov-26, whose key put 50 at the typical listed European company but was anchored on effect size rather than on percentiles; scores tagged rater-v2 or rater-v3 are standings in the Universe.

M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: Structural, non-cyclical volume forces (a 9% value market on biologics, obesity injectables and RTU conversion under 5% penetrated, Annex 1, the FDA draft guidance and BIOSECURE, destocking over) reach nearly all of sales and give about 7-8% volume and mix, net of a direct price give already visible where capacity is loose (RTU vials halved, bulk renewals -5-10%), synchronised syringe capacity from 2028, shrinking vaccines and unhedged currency; consensus sales growth at the 72nd percentile is honest. I sit above the group's 58 because the volume legs are structural and touch the whole business, but below Eckert & Ziegler because the environment supplies no price and its threats fall inside the three-year window.

M:topic:2.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:2.reason: A new CFO and CEO have brought financial discipline to an unchanged strategy: a double-digit-million efficiency programme (about one point of margin by FY2029), pay 30% on free cash flow, nine-month FCF +49%, the customer dispute settled and North Carolina held back, worth a credible capex fall; against that the top commercial executive left for BD, polymer under-use has no plan and retention is missing targets, and none of it steps up earnings power. Gently positive and incremental, like Shell's self-help, so a shade above neutral and above the group's 44, which weighed the earlier target cut that predates this team.

M:topic:3.reason: Qualitatively a concentrated, registration-locked oligopoly (top three over 60%, switching takes months to years, container under 1% of drug cost, 97% repeat revenue) with first places in vials and ampoules, a parent tubing edge and a clean audit record, but the moat protects volume not price, syringe awards are contested as functionally equivalent, and management lowered its goals inside a parent-first KGaA; ROIC of 15.9% (84th percentile) flatters, because the capital added since FY2022 earns about 5% pre-tax and FCF is a quarter of net income. M:topic:5.reason: The structure has plant-level drop-through of 45-55 cents per euro but has realised only about 32 cents since FY2022 as each new site adds fixed cost first, with EBIT leverage near nil as depreciation rose to 8.5% of sales; pricing is index pass-through with no real price taken (gross margin down from 36%), financial leverage is negligible, cost-out is small, and the DCS absorption loop is offset by a balancing capacity loop in DDS syringes. M:topic:1.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:1.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 46
M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: One strong, dated, law-backed tailwind (Dutch grid capex rising from about EUR 10bn to 18bn a year, permit-free substations from late 2027, the SF6 ban Alfen is already certified for) reaches only the grid unit, about 45% of revenue. It comes as volume only, rationed by the operators' technicians and permits (two of three installed 20-30% below plan in 2025), and three monopsony buyers hold its price. Against it, structural headwinds (cell makers selling turnkey, a renewed price war, VAT-rebate removal, charging prices in their seventh quarter of decline as value moves to site owners) act on the two units that make about 60% of gross profit. Consensus sales growth at the 80th percentile reflects the grid volume, but external forces give no support to group margin, so the net is slightly negative over two to three years: negative to mid-2027, mildly positive after. I am a touch above the External change forces group's 44 because the grid force is unusually well funded and dated.

M:topic:2.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:2.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 55
M:topic:2.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:2.reason: Since October 2025 the outside chief executive has run a broad reset and met every dated milestone: three business units, headcount down from 1,053 to 909, EUR 13m of savings, working capital cut from EUR 159m to 58m, DC chargers exited and platforms rationalised, the CATL sodium-ion deal, and UK and Southern European launches. None of it has yet reached margin, EPS or guidance. The 2027 ambition has been cut to 'year-on-year improvement', this is the fourth finance director since January 2024, and the forecasts credit only about EUR 3m of net opex relief in FY27. I sit slightly above the group's 55 because the reset is far broader and better executed than a gentle drift, but the lagging outputs, the open finance seat and a repair rather than growth ambition keep it well short of a 75.

M:topic:3.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:3.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 27
M:topic:3.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:3.reason: The value chain and moat come first. Alfen has one real but buyer-capped moat, about 70% of Dutch secondary substations, but it protects share and not price (the segment's gross-margin target was cut to 20-30%). Two moatless, price-taking hardware units in the sector's losing archetype still make about 60% of gross profit. Management is promising but unproven and has deliberately modest goals. The financial profile then confirms it: ROIC about 0% (9th percentile), EBITDA margin at the 6th percentile, operating margin down 14 points in three years (6th percentile), and new capital earning far below its cost. Only the net-cash balance sheet is sound. Low predictability counts against it too, so I sit inside the four groups (36/36/20/36).

M:topic:4.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 22
M:topic:4.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:4.reason: Since 2023 every guidance move has been a cut or a withdrawal: three consecutive mid-year revenue cuts (-12%, -22%, -8%) and no raise under the new chief executive. The 2026 beats were storage timing; the 2025 misses were demand. FY26 revenue guidance is conservative, but the margin midpoint (needing about EUR 8.6m of H2 EBITDA against an evidenced EUR 1.9m) is not. Management steers candidly in words but has let half the brokers stay above the evidence, which matches the Guidance group's 24 and sits a little below the Sell-side group's 32.

M:topic:5.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:5.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 62
M:topic:5.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:5.reason: This scores the structure. Operating leverage is real and proven both ways: a 26-27% contribution margin on about EUR 100m of largely personnel opex, plus EUR 23-24m of fixed charges below EBITDA, so 10% more or less revenue moves EBITDA 40-50% (the same EUR 440m of revenue gave 18% EBITDA in FY22 and 5.9% in FY25). The other gears are absent or negative: prices fall in charging, follow cells in storage and are capped in grid; there is no financial leverage; the big cost-out is already in the base; and the feedback loops run mostly negative. Opex inflation also eats about a third of the drop-through, so the forecast EPS-to-revenue ratio from a near-zero base overstates the gearing. That is above the level-50 mix on gearing alone, but well short of Judges Scientific's 72-type proven leverage with stable pricing.

M:topic:6.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:6.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 66
M:topic:6.measure: Forecast adjusted EPS from EUR -0.13 (FY26) and 0.06 (FY27) to EUR 0.60 (FY30): compound growth far above 35% a year from a near-zero base
M:topic:6.letter_rule: fixed: the Rater's letter from Richard's cut-offs on the measure (never re-cut); the number sits inside the letter's band
M:topic:6.reason: Above 35% gives C. I place it at the bottom of the band because the growth is the mechanical spreading of EUR 23-24m of fixed charges over a recovering EBITDA from a trough, not a strong business. Revenue grows only about 6.5% a year, all organic and grid-led, and the EBITDA margin reaches only 6.9% by FY30 against 11-18% in FY21-23. That is better than the last four years but well below the company's past, and full-definition FCF is about nil.

M:topic:7.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:7.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 13
M:topic:7.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:7.reason: Over the next 6-12 months the likely changes are all downward. FY26 guidance is more likely met at the floor or missed (about 30% below the floor) than raised, and any FY27 range given in February is more likely to be steered down later than raised. Consensus faces three documented cut steps: FY26 EBITDA about -15% (75% likely), FY27 EPS -40 to -60% on the D&A line (70%), and FY27 EBITDA about -10% (65%). Against growth of about 5% a year these are ratios of several times minus one. The narrative has already capitulated (0% buys), which limits further damage, and an upside branch of about one in three keeps it off the floor; the fourth-set group's 18 agrees.

M:topic:9.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:9.reason: The memo's FY27 EPS cone (-0.26 to +0.38 around 0.06) spans losses to profits, and the EBITDA cone (EUR 16-34m) is about a third either way, resolving only by August 2027. Risks are sudden and material: storage intake has swung from EUR 54m to 11m in a quarter, trading updates are binary, 7.6% of the capital is short and the stock has a 1.24 beta to a de-rating sector. Two customers are 34.8% of revenue on frameworks with no minimum volumes, and there is one cell supplier and one plant. The 2023-25 quality failure and the sector precedents favour caution. Net cash, low solvency risk and good operating disclosure keep it above the leveraged cases, so I sit below the groups' 28 and 38 because the cone spans the zero line.

M:topic:10.reason: I agree with the memo, not the computed Reinforcing. The price ran a false turn-up in spring 2026 (+53%) and has stalled since (-48%), while earnings are still bottoming (H2 2026 at a 1% margin, H1 2027 below the prior year) and estimates are about to be cut. M:topic:11.letter_rule: fixed: the Rater's letter from Richard's cut-offs on the measure (never re-cut); the number sits inside the letter's band
M:topic:11.reason: Dear on one measure and neutral on the other gives D. The neutral reading flatters, because it rests on consensus EPS the memo shows is about 85% too high; on the forecasts' EPS the P/E is 52.8x, above the 90th percentile. On EV/EBITDA the shares are about 39% below their own history, but that cheapness is largely deserved by the mix change and the stalling phase. The memo's fair value (26x, or 9x FY28 EBITDA, about EUR 11.5) sits roughly 11% above the price, so I place it in the upper middle of the band rather than at its floor.

M:topic:12.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 48
M:topic:12.measure: About +7% probability-weighted to end-2027: the memo's +11% at its 9x EBITDA / 26x P/E fair multiple (+24% at 10x), weighed against -16% at the 7x trough and -37% on a further FY27 cut; the model's +92% is a P/E artefact and is set aside
M:topic:12.letter_rule: fixed: the Rater's letter from Richard's cut-offs on the measure (never re-cut); the number sits inside the letter's band
M:topic:12.reason: About +7% sits in D, which maps to about 42. I place it at 41, a point lower, because two forces offset each other: the lower tail is fat and comes first (three downgrade steps before any upgrade), while the three-year check is supportive (+55% to +70% if grid volume delivers, flat if it grows only 5% a year). Nothing comes from dividends or buybacks.

M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: Demand is not the problem (US regional gaming revenue +2.5% to +3.6%, UK online +10% to +13%), but every enacted or live external force on the business moves against it: UK Remote Gaming Duty 21% to 40% and Betting Duty to 25% (about EUR 120m gross at the subsidiary), Chicago's video gaming terminals now licensed at 78 sites diluting the flagship's exclusivity, PENN's doubled Aurora capacity, and credit markets pricing Bally's at 11% to 13%; the one tailwind, UK consolidation, sits in a 58%-owned ring-fenced subsidiary and is already in its margin recovery. No figure in figures.md measures this directly; coherent with the External change forces group at 20, I place it just below BP (a structural drag on the main earnings line) and above Yara, because demand itself holds.

M:topic:2.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:2.reason: The real operating positives (North America Interactive at breakeven, the Baton Rouge and Marquette conversions, the subsidiary's 65% duty mitigation, the Chicago structure topped off) are worth tens of millions, are back-ended and half leak to minorities, while control is concentrated in the sponsor as Executive Chair, the finance function is hollowed out (three CFO changes, no treasurer, a material weakness, two late filings) and debt-funded deals (Sam's Town, the USD 500m Bronx licence) contradict the stated capital preservation; the decisive change is a sponsor-led capital-structure event likelier to crystallise minority losses than to cure them. A self-inflicted repair on dilutive terms is the 10 level; coherent with the group's 14, I place it between TT Electronics (leadership churn and a restatement, with some recovery) and Alfen (covenant breached, targets withdrawn), nearer Alfen because a going-concern note now sits on top.

M:topic:3.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)

M:topic:3.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:3.reason: Qualitatively the industry is sound (licence-capped local oligopolies, rational rivals) and Rhode Island is a real moat to 2043, but Bally's sits in the squeezed middle of its chain (landlord, lenders, slot makers and fiscal authorities take the value), Chicago's moat is being diluted before it opens, the UK and lottery moats are 58% owned, US online has none, maintenance capex runs at 4.4% of casino revenue against a 6% to 8% norm and the management serves the controlling holder (guidance abandoned, pay discretionary). The figures tell the truth and are worse than BP's: ROIC -11.5% (2nd percentile), operating margin 1.1% (6th), net debt to EBITDA 16.1x (99th, worst), free cash flow negative since FY2021, and the new capital (Chicago, the Bronx) is forecast to earn below its 8.5% to 13% cost for years; coherent with the groups (30, 27, 4, 9), I place it below BP and above SMA, which lacks even Bally's local protections.

M:topic:5.reason: The structure has real operating gearing at property level (Casinos & Resorts flow-through about 55%) and extreme financial gearing (equity about eight times geared to EV), but the gears point the wrong way: fixed charges rise from USD 725m to 884m in FY2027 while EBITDAR barely moves, Chicago's USD 80m rent lands before its earnings, B2C's incremental margin fell from about 50% to 30% under the duty, there is no pricing power at the parent, the cuttable pool is USD 30m to 60m, and the dominant loop is a debt-funded deficit adding USD 40m to 60m of interest a year so that revenue growth gives wider losses through FY2028. The forecast ratio is meaningless (losses throughout); this is close to the 10 level (leverage stretched and running in reverse, no cost-out that matters), held a little above it because the same gearing would amplify a strong Chicago ramp and USD 85m a year of the interest is non-cash accretion.

M:topic:1.reason: Three real external forces (scarce virgin fibre with kraftliner up EUR 200/t, Swedish wood down 15-20% after the storm, self-generated energy against a gas spike) lift the price-cost spread through about mid-2027. Against them sit dated direct threats (salvage wood ending, 1.45Mt of UK recycled capacity from March 2027, oversupplied cartonboard) and structural drags (graphic paper, 22% of sales, shrinking 5% a year; demand only refill at about 1% growth), so over two to three years the net is a small, front-loaded positive, coherent with the External change forces group at 54, above Kerry's neutral environment and below OEM International's modestly positive one.

M:topic:2.reason: Self-help is proven and material for the size of today's earnings: the SEK 800m programme (SEK 550m in 2026, the rest in 2027, its predecessor closed a year early), the Escanaba cancellation, two capex cuts and new operator regional presidents supply about SEK 0.45bn of the 2027 increase, and the North American packaging ramp is on track. But it is repair of a cyclical business, not an engine (SEK 2.3bn of savings since 2023 left EBITDA where it started), and it is netted by a dividend cut, no buyback at 0.55x book, a defensive Gavle boiler call of SEK 3bn or more, overrunning North American shutdowns and the strategic-projects head leaving, so it sits just above Shell's incremental self-help and below Odfjell Drilling, in line with the group's 57.

M:topic:3.reason: The niches are real (global number two in liquid packaging board with two-to-four-year qualification, number two in European sack paper and fluting, a tariff-protected, low-wood-cost North American business), but the group owns under 5% of its wood, is the marginal-cost producer in its European grades so price follows its own wood cost, has more than half its costs in kronor against 80% foreign revenue, and sits in the two least profitable stages of the chain; management is competent and disciplined but defensive. The financial profile confirms it rather than misleading: ROIC 2.1% (18th percentile), operating margin 2.6% (8th), EPS down 48% a year over three years (4th), with returns forecast at only 5-7% to 2030, below the cost of capital, and only the 1.6x leverage keeps it off the floor; this matches the groups (45, 36, 26, 52) and places it just below CVS Group and above Solid State.

M:topic:5.reason: Operating leverage is very high in structure: fixed depreciation of about 7% of sales leaves operating profit at about 4%, the incremental margin on price and wood is about 100%, and mill curtailments make volume losses worse than proportional, so 2027 EPS roughly quadruples on under 3% revenue growth. M:topic:9.reason: The case is simple to model (three published sensitivities explain about 90% of pre-tax variance; balance-sheet lines are guided with dates) but the memo's cone is plus or minus 45-50% on FY2027-28 EPS, driven by two external prices that re-price in days (Brent fell 16% in three days), with the sector's highest refining and trading gearing, a 1.18 beta to a sector near the top of its multiple range, untrackable trading and capture lines and a buyback BP has failed to hold twice in six years; the repaired balance sheet protects dividend and credit, not the share price. Coherent with the risk groups' 26 and 30: a single exogenous-input case with a range well over a third either way, at Fugro's cyclical-outlook risk and below Entra.

M:topic:1.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:1.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 62.0
M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: Two external legs reach most of sales: a broad Nordic construction turn still feeding 2027 revenue through the two-to-four-quarter lag (Swedish production +9% in 2026, starts +8%, Q2 intake +44%) and SEK 7-8bn of contracted data-centre work (about 10% of FY2027 revenue) with defence, transport and EPBD lengthening the tail; they are trimmed by margin headwinds (wages, copper, 15 bidders per tender, a second qualified data-centre bidder) and a rate turn that bites in 2028. Above Richard's 66 as he ruled (Swedish macro turning and data-centre build-outs) and coherent with the group's 70: more than Instalco's recovery alone, short of Helios Towers' structural, multi-year demand.

M:topic:2.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:2.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 50.0
M:topic:2.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:2.reason: A completed, dated clean-up (Denmark from 0.1% to 5.1% and holding, the Swedish merger on budget with SEK 65m of savings, Finland's branch closures worth SEK 60-75m by FY2028, ABEKA sold, a rebuilt CFO/Sweden/M&A layer, the first buybacks) plus a genuinely new move into principal-contractor data-centre work, worth about 3-5% of EPS by FY2027 beyond what is in the base; offset by a stalled acquisition engine, 77% cash conversion, no internal audit and undated, never-met targets (the turnkey write-down risk is scored in topic 9). Above Richard's 48 and a little above the group's 57, because the data-centre capability is a large strategic move, but short of a full reset with growth on top.

M:topic:3.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:3.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 45.0
M:topic:3.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:3.reason: A defensible position without an economic moat: Nordic number two in a fragmented market (top five about 18%) where the tail sets price, with density, a 48% indexed service franchise (91% renewal) and rare complex-project capability, but gross margin stuck at 14-15% and EBITA at 5.2-6.9% for ten years (operating margin percentile 22) against peers at 7-8%; ROIC 12% (percentile 74) on capex under 1% of sales and 0.9x leverage is real, and the team is above median but has never delivered its margin target. Above Richard's 52 (not a poor business) and coherent with the groups' 54-60; beside MITIE (54) on its levels, above Vodafone but below Helios Towers' improving unit economics.

M:topic:4.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:4.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 32.0
M:topic:4.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:4.reason: No short-term guidance; the undated 7% margin target has been missed for over ten years, the informal 'close to 7% in FY2026' has slipped to about 6.4% and all three operating targets were missed in FY2025, while volume beats in upswings (Q2 2026 EBITA +11% against consensus) are followed 12-18 months later by project-margin misses (2023, Q3 2025, FY2025 EPS consensus -5.8%); consensus now sits above every target and the company does nothing to steer it. Kept about 45 as Richard ruled and coherent with the groups' 42-44: slightly above Instalco, which missed every FY2025 target, below Sdiptech's newly set targets.

M:topic:5.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:5.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 38.0
M:topic:5.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:5.reason: About 90% of the cost base is variable (fixed costs 8-9%), price is nominal with a 9-12 month lag on unindexed Swedish contracts, financial leverage is trivial and cost-out is SEK 65m plus perhaps SEK 30-60m; the incremental margin of about 11% is idle capacity being refilled and fades to about 9% during 2027, and the data-centre reference loop is capped at two large projects. The model's EPS-to-revenue ratio of about 1.8x (FY2025-29 EPS +9.9% a year against revenue +5.5%) comes from savings, the Finnish fix, buybacks and a trough base, not from operating gearing, which resolves the contradiction Richard flagged: low gearing here and the same 90% variable costs narrowing the downside in topic 9; coherent with the Financial forecasts group (52) only on that reading.

M:topic:6.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:6.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 55.0
M:topic:6.measure: Model adjusted EPS compound growth of about 9.9% a year over the four forecast years FY2025A to FY2029 (SEK 6.03 to 8.80); FY2026-30 gives about 7.1%
M:topic:6.letter_rule: fixed: the Rater's letter from Richard's cut-offs on the measure (never re-cut); the number sits inside the letter's band
M:topic:6.reason: The measure sits at the top of the 5-10% portion of C, but I place it in the middle of the band because the growth is a front-loaded, cycle-driven step (+17%, +14%, then +7% and +3%, consensus two-to-three-year EPS growth at the 5th percentile) and the margin path improves only about 70bp on a flat ten-year envelope without reaching 7%. It is organic plus about 1% a year of buybacks, with acquisitions at a trough, so the growth is honest but not compounding.

M:topic:7.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:7.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 30.0
M:topic:7.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:7.reason: There is no guidance to raise, and on the memo's event path consensus may edge up 0-3% at the Q3 and Q4 prints (stale July brokers, a dividend above SEK 4.00, definitional reported-EPS beats) before falling from May 2027 as drop-through fades, wages reset and the cash trough arrives: about 50% odds of FY2027 EPS lower by more than 3% in twelve months against 25% higher, and FY2028 at a 7.1% margin more exposed; against about 11% revenue growth the expected change is around -0.2 to -0.3x, with a narrative that knows the upside and not the downside. Coherent with the group's 30 but a little above it for the near-term beats: below IMCD's limited scope, about TT Electronics' flattered revisions.

M:topic:12.reason: About +13% sits in the C band (10-20%), about 57 on the scale; the three-year check of about +48% is supportive but comes entirely from Evoke's synergy-geared earnings leg and a recovery of the multiple. Moved down to 52 for the fat lower tail: the standalone and no-completion cases (-18%, 15% weight) and the absorbed case (-15%) carry 28% of the weight, and the balance-sheet and owner tail (an equity issuance at EUR 0.80, a fair-trough value of EUR 0.49-0.60) lies outside the weighted figure.

M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: The external forces take from growth and margins over two to three years: beer about two-thirds of volume and structurally flat (footprint +0.3% a year, Western Europe -4% in H1 and Q3 2026), China volume -6% and -10% in the quarters that carry two-thirds of its profit with part of the loss share and channel, rule-driven mainstream price competition in the UK and Poland, dated regulation (Vietnamese excise, UK deposit scheme and sugar threshold) and a 2027 input-cost round of about 160bp of gross margin; the real external positives (soft drinks and alcohol-free growth, India, easy Chinese comparatives from Q2 2027, inflation-linked price pass-through in a rational oligopoly) only partly offset, and the PepsiCo licence wins and the Kazakhstan volume are the company's own and scored in topic 2. Consensus sales growth at the 31st percentile fits a clearly but not severely negative environment, just below Entra's mild negative and above Vodafone's, coherent with the External change forces group at 35.

M:topic:2.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:2.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 63
M:topic:2.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:2.reason: A broad, resourced and largely delivered programme: Britvic closed and its synergies running ahead (about 30% in year one against 10-15%, target raised to GBP 110m), Southeast Asia's 25% sold at 21.3x EBIT, the Kazakhstan plant opened on schedule, PepsiCo territories added, the executive team rebuilt and leverage cut from 3.9x to 3.0x in a year, which together take EPS growth from about 3% a year to about 8% with a dated buyback ahead; it is held back by Britvic earning below its cost of capital (about 5-7%), earnings quality in transition (DKK 1.9bn of special items, the hybrid, rising minorities), weaker working capital and a revenue algorithm never met, and the self-help fades after 2027. I place it a little above the Internal change forces group's 64 because whether the effect is already in consensus belongs to topic 7, not here; it sits between OEM International's acquisition-led change and Theon's growth pivot.

M:topic:3.reason: A concentrated, rational oligopoly with excise passed through and inelastic demand, and real local moats (number one or two in 25 markets carrying about 70% of volume, on-trade lock-in, multi-beverage density), run by an operator that delivers its profit every year; but Carlsberg is third of three and a challenger in 66% of its volume, its pricing power is nominal, its cost of goods is well above AB InBev's, and new capital (Britvic at about 5-7%) earns below its cost while minorities leak profit from the best regions. M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: The force that reaches the profit pool is structural and mandated: camera fitment from 49% to 60% of windscreens under EU GSR2, recalibration adding EUR 150-300 a job, a US claims-frequency recovery from 1.5% against a 2.1% average, the State Farm programme and a rising technical bar squeezing independents, plus PHE's ageing parc and TVH's recovery. Netted against it are the direct threats: US insurers starting to cap calibration and NAGS mark-ups, a mild El Nino winter, a weak US consumer, and a collapsing Belgian car market at Automotive, which falls from 17% to about 7% of profit. I sit above the group score of 56 because that score was anchored on flat group revenue, which is Automotive's shrinkage, while the profit-weighted balance is about 60/40 positive. That puts it a clear but offset positive, just above Linea Directa (a pricing cycle exposed to reversal) and below Eckert & Ziegler.

M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: A structural, multi-year channel migration (online about 3% of US and 7% of UK pouch sales against 36% in Sweden, users crossing the 7-8 pouches-a-day threshold), a category growing about 21% a year, state taxes pushing heavy users online and manufacturer rivalry buying visibility support 13-16% revenue growth for years with low cyclicality; consensus sales growth at the 96th percentile is flattered by the ZYN base effect, and the forces are trimmed by direct threats to them (supplier control of supply, a possible EU cross-border ban, US fines, the larger ZYN can) and give weaker support to profit. Close to the External change forces group's 72: a strong, visible leg reaching most of revenue but trimmed, so just below Helios Towers.

M:topic:2.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:2.reason: The internal force is one lever: cost restraint on a finished build-out (systems migration, four automated warehouses, perimeter tidied) after marketing rose from 1.0% to 3.2% of sales and was found largely wasteful; if held it drives most of the forecast 2027 EBITDA gain, but it is evidenced by one admission and one flat quarter, against a 2026 overspend, recurring items and compliance costs. I sit a little above the Internal change forces group's 50 because the build-out is funded and complete and the restraint is rational rather than forced, but it is gently positive and unproven, below Shell's evidenced self-help-plus.

M:topic:3.reason: Qualitatively above average: about 14 times the next online rival, about 97% unpaid traffic, data and media sold to manufacturers, compliance as a barrier and habitual, non-cyclical demand (Industry 70, Competitive advantage 66); but the hostile force is the strongest one, three suppliers holding about 87% of volume, there is no consumer pricing power, and the Growth build-out has so far earned a negative return. The financial profile is weak (ROIC 5.9%, 44th percentile; operating margin at the 9th; reported EPS under 42% of adjusted; thin free cash flow; Economic strength 33) and management misses its financial promises (Management 45), so predictability pulls a high-quality core down to a medium-quality whole, level with Shell and below Helios Towers' proven unit economics.

M:topic:5.reason: The structure has large operating leverage (variable costs above gross profit only about 2% of sales, so an extra krona contributes 16-18 ore against a 4-6% EBITDA margin), supplier-side pricing power (supplier-paid income carries almost no direct cost), fixed-cost absorption on a platform built for twice the volume and a SEK 110-130m cost cushion; but there is no consumer pricing power or financial leverage, and the gearing has not been harvested (15% of extra gross profit kept in 2025, none in 2026), the case Richard warns of, so the forecast EPS-to-revenue ratio of about 3.5 times is promised rather than proven. M:topic:1.reason: The structural force is grocers moving own-label protein to a few scaled contract packers (UK own-label above half, Ahold to 45%, Walmart diversifying from the big four packers), and plant-based has been disproved; but beef supply tightens to 2028 (Australian slaughter -6% then -9%), trade-down cut West core-meat profit 20.5% on flat volume, Tesco is moving streams to integrated processors, and UK wages and a weak post-Budget consumer pass through with a lag. Consensus sales growth at the 30th percentile fits; net mildly negative over 18 months and about neutral over three years on the existing estate (the new-country wins are counted in topic 2), so just above Carlsberg's modest mature environment and below Tenaris's mixed one, in line with the group's 42.

M:topic:1.reason: Three external legs reach most of the business: the AI data-centre build (Data Center organic +44% in Q3, optical demand about 20% a year to 2031), the US private-fibre rebuild with BEAD orders landing from 2027 (North America 48% of sales, +80%), and defence. They are cyclical rather than contracted, their rate of change peaked in Q3 2026, and they are trimmed by direct threats: the glass and connector cap, US HDPE duct price pressure and a structurally shrinking European duct market, so 2027 organic growth is about 9% against 17% now. That is a clear multi-part positive, a little above the External change forces group's 68 because it reaches most of sales, but short of Helios Towers' structural, visible demand; it sits just above Eckert & Ziegler.

M:topic:2.reason: The external CEO's change is large, broad and already in the accounts. He beat the SEK 120m cost programme (SEK 110m target), pivoted Data Center and Harsh Environment from 27% to 44% of sales, bought three bolt-ons at 5-6x, raised SEK 600m, signed the NKT subsea framework that doubles capacity from 2028, and lifted the Fiber Solutions margin from 5.4% to 9.4%. Against it, the self-help is now finished and the bench has thinned (deputy CEO gone, an acting Data Center head, no CFO successor named), and there are four commissioning slips. I sit above the group's 67 because the pivot is a large strategic move whose outputs are already reaching profit; the thinning bench and the end of repair keep it below NKT and just above Theon.

M:topic:1.reason: The 2026 lift came from forces that are reversing on a schedule: DSV's integration distraction (its recapture is planned over three to four quarters), Red Sea and Hormuz diversions holding yields up (Suez transits already at 58-59% of 2023), tariff front-loading, and a container delivery wave of 3.1m TEU in 2027 and 4.4m in 2028 against demand of about 4%. Those take unit gross profit down 4-5% a year, while lasting positives (customs complexity, technology and cloud demand, volume at or above the market) are smaller. Consensus sales growth at the 21st percentile and 3-year growth at the 4th agree. This is a scarcity price unwinding, but it hits a forwarder's yield, not a carrier's whole earnings, so the company sits well above Maersk; I am coherent with the group's 33.

M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: The external forces roughly cancel and tilt slightly negative over two to three years. The incumbents' price umbrella (market motor price +4% to 6%, non-life premiums +5.5% to 6%, Spanish GDP 2%+) lifts volume, but claims-cost growth of 3.5% to 4.5% (Baremo 3.3% to 3.5%, parts +5.1%), Mutua's open-ended tariff freeze, and Mapfre's and AXA's turn to volume from 2027 squeeze the 2027 margin and bring a soft-market risk forward to 2028. The 78th-percentile consensus sales growth is mostly price inflation, and the 2022 to 2023 loss shows how a severity step lands. This is a touch below the External change forces group's 50 because the soft-market threat now falls inside the window, and it sits between Kerry's neutral environment and Indutrade's soft backdrop.

M:topic:2.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:2.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was None
M:topic:2.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:2.reason: The internal change is a continuing, well-executed but narrowing programme. The expense ratio fell from 22.1% to 19.4%, solvency was rebuilt to 191.5%, the dividend was restored and raised, guidance was raised twice in words and health moves to a new network in 2027. But there is no new lever, the next one (capital policy and disclosure) is unused, and incentives favour volume over margin, the reserve buffer has been lowered from the 95th to the 85th percentile and control weaknesses are rising. Profit growth of 35% this year is the end of the repricing recovery, not a new force. This is Richard's 'gently positive but mediocre' case (CVS 55), coherent with the group's 53, and it sits between Shell's incremental self-help and Hexatronic.

M:topic:3.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:3.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was None
M:topic:3.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:3.reason: On the qualitative parts: the market is concentrated, compulsory and high-barrier, but its price discipline depends on a mutual price-setter (industry group 50). The cost advantage is real and structural, a 7-to-8-point expense gap that has held through a full cycle, but it is narrow, with low switching costs and softer advantages that are narrowing (competitive advantage 57). Management is a capable but inward-facing operator team (50). The financial profile is strong and clean (ROIC 22.4%, 92nd percentile; ROE 82nd percentile; no debt; no goodwill; growth needs only about EUR 35m a year, so new capital earns well above its cost). But predictability is low: the combined ratio took the pre-tax margin from 19.6% to a loss on a 9% revenue move, and reserve development is opaque. On balance it is above average but short of Carlsberg's franchise, and it sits between Carlsberg and Indutrade.

But the record includes a severe FY22 to FY23 miss (combined ratio 104%) in the claims-inflation environment now recurring. Guidance is verbal and outcome-only, and the company does nothing to keep consensus conservative: FY27 consensus sits about 6% above deliverable, while the 'low 90s' guide will be met. M:topic:5.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)

M:topic:5.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:5.reason: The structure has little upside gearing. About 55% of the expense base is fixed, but expenses are only about 20 points of a 92% combined ratio, so drop-through is about 0.1 point of ratio per 1% of growth, and most of that is reinvested in price. Pricing power is relative: the company follows the market up at a churn cost and cannot lead it. It has no financial leverage, cost-out is gradual (EUR 12m to 15m pre-tax by FY28) and the cost-price-volume loop is weakening. Forecast EPS grows about 1.1 times revenue against a typical 2 times. The large combined-ratio sensitivity is symmetric and external, so it is a risk (topic 9), not a gear. Profit grows roughly with revenue, which is the 25 to 50 level description, beside Bravida (36) and AQ Group (34).

M:topic:5.reason: The structure has real gearing: a 60-65% contribution margin and largely committed cost base, a shrinking fixed financing cost (27% of operating profit in FY2027, 15% in FY2030) that amplifies EPS, three to five points of defensive cost-out, and a reinforcing training-TOUCH-plates-distributor loop; the model turns 14% revenue growth into about 35% EPS growth. But it is unproven and asymmetric: incremental EBITDA margins of 15-21.5% because beats are reinvested while shortfalls drop through at 50-60%, plating price flat to down (pricing power only on TOUCH in the US), and a negative loop where the working-capital build abroad absorbs cash and inflates tax. Above the asymmetric 50s on the fixed-cost structure and financial leverage, short of the 75s where two gears are proven.

M:topic:1.reason: External forces are a mild net positive over two to three years: the statutory wage shock is fading (net inflation drag down to £10m-12m), demand indicators are at records (pipeline £32.5bn, order intake +33%, renewals 91%) and regulation, decarbonisation, water and data centres give multi-year compliance and projects demand, but the UK market grows only 2-3%, the Public Interest Test reaches an exposed public book of about £800m-1bn from FY29, automation deflates hours-billed work and edge competition costs about 30bp on public renewals. Consensus sales growth at the 52nd percentile fits a typical, slightly positive environment; I agree with the group's 54 and lift it marginally for the margin relief in FY27-28, placing it just below Instalco's recovering end-market and above Tenaris's mixed one (the bid premium is not an operating-environment force and is not counted here).

M:topic:2.reason: EQT's control has turned a cash accumulator into a self-funded serial acquirer (seven deals in twelve months adding about 9% of sales at about 0.95x sales, earn-outs revalued up, so it is working), with a new board, deputy CEO and cash-focused CFO and a probable leverage framework still to come, which is a large strategic move adding about half of EPS growth from 2028. M:topic:1.reason: External forces are a clear, multi-part, structural net positive on the 88% of revenue outside Exhibitions: professionals using AI still need trusted data, so database owners keep customers and charge more at renewal (peers confirm it: Thomson Reuters Legal at 9-10%, Karnov AI tiers at +30%), law-firm IT spend doubled from 2% to 4% of revenue, STM demand rose from 4% to 6%, and falling model and token costs help margins. Against that sit a funded and direct threat at the Legal workflow layer (Harvey, Legora, Google), a cyclical Middle East dip in Exhibitions and small grant-rule and print drags; consensus sales growth at the 75th percentile is honest, but group organic growth is steady at about 7% rather than accelerating, so this is above Spie's favourable-but-mixed reading and below Helios Towers' broad structural pull, a touch above the 66 External change forces group because the forces reach nearly the whole perimeter.

M:topic:3.reason: None of the four parts is ordinary. The structure is number one or two everywhere, with an 85-90% US legal-research duopoly, near-monopoly contributory data in Risk and unpaid or powerless suppliers. The moats (curated content licensed even by the entrants, retention above 95%) are widening under AI, and returns on new capital are above 30%, which the figures confirm (ROIC 24.8% at the 94th percentile, margins at the 82nd to 84th, cash conversion 99%) and which are among the most predictable in Europe. Management has a sixteen-year record of delivery. I sit above the 78-80 groups because all four are strong at once and predictability adds to the quality, and I deduct for the contested legal interface (about an eighth of profit), the limited room to reinvest and the open succession; that puts it above Reply and Avanza, well short of ASML's monopoly bottleneck.

M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: Defence (47% of FY26 revenue) gets a funded, structural UK and NATO budget rise, and the 20/40/40 doctrine points it at Steatite's and Custom Power's products. The industrial destock has ended, and AI data-centre and US autonomy demand add a small third leg. These are offset by direct threats that are certain sooner: DRAM and component inflation, a £28bn Treasury funding gap with CMA screening that lengthens awards, the US continuing resolution, and unhedged dollar purchasing. I put it above the External change forces group (63) because this is a clear multi-part positive reaching most of sales, but below a 75 because the restock is a pulse and the defence money turns into contracts on a contested calendar.

M:topic:3.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)

M:topic:3.reason: Accreditation and design-in give a genuine but narrow moat on about 60% of revenue (Systems and Power). Against it: 39% is moatless distribution at a 4% margin, there is a sole-source channel dependency on Persistent with undisclosed terms, one customer is 17% of revenue, pricing power is only cost recovery, and the capacity built recently is under-used, so the return on new capital is still unproven. The figures confirm it: operating margin at the 17th percentile, ROIC 5.6% (42nd), EPS falling for three years (16th), with strong cash conversion and a near-net-cash balance sheet as the offsets. Low predictability keeps it in line with the groups (42 to 52), below IMCD's real specialty moat and above Teqnion's sub-par acquired returns.

M:topic:5.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)

M:topic:5.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:5.reason: Operating leverage is large and proven both ways. A £42m fixed overhead on a 33.5% gross margin puts break-even at about £110m to £115m; FY25's 23% revenue fall cut operating profit 65%, and each £10m of Systems revenue now adds about £3m of operating profit. The base case has EPS growing about 2.5 times as fast as revenue. It stays below 75 because the other gears are missing: pricing is only cost recovery, financial leverage is immaterial, cost-out is small and the loops are slow. And, as Richard warns, the gearing disappointed on the way up in FY26, when 70% of the gross-profit gain was reinvested in overhead.

M:topic:3.reason: The qualitative parts are good but not exceptional. Germany is a fragmented market that SPIE consolidates and France is a rational oligopoly where SPIE is only number four. Moderate, mostly widening advantages come from prequalified grid and nuclear crews, a recruiting edge, frameworks with retention above 90%, and -34 days of working capital that funds growth. Management is disciplined but risk-averse, with organic growth averaging 1.8%. The Universe figures understate the financial profile: gross margin (pct 6), EBITDA margin (pct 19) and ROIC of 4.1% (pct 30) reflect a labour-services model and EUR 4.4bn of goodwill. Cash conversion (pct 93), returns on tangible capital above 50% and margins at the top of the peer group are the truer reading, though Deutsche Bank's 9.1% return on cumulative acquisition spend is only about the cost of capital and 56% of costs go to subcontracting. I place it in line with the groups (55 to 63), a little above the comparable MITIE (54) and just below Linea Directa (64).

M:master:foundations_robustness.because: Rating = 72 (standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies), set by the Rater. The business is good rather than elite (topic 3, 63): a fragmented German market it consolidates, a rational French oligopoly and a stack of moderate moats. What lifts the foundations above that, as with Richard's CVS, is stability: 85% of revenue visible at the start of the year, 70-75% maintenance, retention above 90%, margins up every year since 2020, cash conversion above 100% in every year but one since 2015, and a floor-and-beat delivery record on the lines it guides (topic 4, 68). It is held below 75 by the 56% subcontracted cost base, a 9.1% return on cumulative acquisition spend, goodwill of EUR 4.4bn and recurrent organic misses.

M:master:setups_fit.because: Rating = 58 (standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies), set by the Rater. The case is recognisably 'cause for concern clearing in a quality, low-cyclicality business on a low multiple', but two elements are loose in substance. The concern is exogenous (French sovereign yields), not something in the business that is being repaired. And the multiple is low only against two years; against ten years it sits at the 49th percentile, at the median. A small current problem also blurs the fit: the company's own financing has diluted EPS, and the ROFA price is unverified. The timing of the EPS cut is left to topics 7 and 12. That places it below the 65-75 Richard gave CVS for a major concern clearing.

M:master:case_riskiness.because: Rating = 63 (standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies), set by the Rater. Topic 9 (64) carries it. The fundamental risks are mostly 'paper cuts': a narrow EBITA cone, contractual below-EBITA items, low fixed-rate leverage and shallow cyclicality. Unlike Richard's CVS, though, the share price is governed by a dated political binary outside the company's control. EPS consensus is too high and the company is not managing it down. ROFA adds a new cyclical automotive line at an unreconciled price, and a crowded buy side could amplify a quantified bear note. That puts it above Arteche's 60, whose risk was a high multiple, but well short of the 80s.

M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: Industry (43% of sales) is in a real short-cycle upturn (PMIs at four-year highs, organic sales +4-6%, 19-21% incremental margin) and the acquisition market is structurally kind (deep succession-driven supply, rational 6-8x pricing), but Swedish construction (a fifth to a quarter of the group) has not turned, Nordic consumer retail is destocking and a Riksbank hike lifts the cost of floating debt and weighs on construction; no figure in figures.md isolates this, and consensus sales growth of 4.2% (p40) fits a mixed environment. A mild net positive, a little above the group's 50 because the deal market is an external positive for a serial acquirer, just above Tenaris and well short of Instalco's clean end-market turn.

M:topic:2.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)

M:topic:2.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:2.reason: A multi-part internal reset is largely delivered and already reaching earnings (leverage 4.35x to 2.3-2.5x, refinancing with maturities to 2030, net financial items cut from SEK 1,044m to a run-rate of about 630m, 20-plus loss-makers sold, parent costs halved, SEK 738m of puts settled so the minority leakage shrinks), and the acquisition engine has been relit (17 deals at 6.5-7.0x, a pivot to B2B and non-Swedish niches), but the engine runs at a fraction of the needed scale and Services has had three heads in a year with the M&A head as interim and no internal audit; the -10% three-year EPS growth (p24) reflects the pre-repair years, not today's forces. I sit above the group's 57 because the repair's outputs are banked rather than modest, and just below OEM's engine-led change because Storskogen's growth leg is still unproven.

M:topic:1.reason: The external swing is large and near-term: US seamless pricing up 26% this year, lean distributor stocks, imports falling and a 30% deepwater step-up in 2027, adding about 10% to FY2027 revenue and most of a $565m EBITDA step. But the biggest leg is a policy-and-refill price rent that Section 232 bargaining or a full restocking can end. The only structural leg, deepwater, is about a fifth of sales, and input costs, the Hormuz deferral and weak South American onshore offset part, so over two to three years the net positive fades to flat revenue in 2028 and a fall in 2029. I agree with the group's 64 and put it a little above Linea Directa's advanced, reversible cycle, but below Eckert & Ziegler's structural demand.

M:topic:11.reason: Neutral on one measure and dear on the other gives D. The neutral reading flatters, because the ten-year range is lifted by trough-earnings multiples of 20-35x, while peak-delivery years traded at 6-9x and 13x sits at the 89th percentile of five years. Part of the cohort premium is deserved (net cash, Rig Direct, dividend), and the memo's own fair 12-13x is about today's multiple, so I place it in the lower-middle of the band.

M:topic:1.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:1.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 82
M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: European rearmament floored by policy to 2035, sovereign-content rules that hard-code Theon's eligibility, agency procurement funnelling awards to the largest qualified supplier and a 1.46 EURbn backlog make demand structural and visible (consensus sales growth p95 is honest, not a one-off); netted against the direct threats to those forces, the external tube cap that slows night-vision growth to 4-7% after FY2027 and agency buyer power on price. I place it a notch above the External change forces group's 76 because rates, credit spreads and sector de-rating act on the multiple, not on organic growth or margins, and just below Arteche, with Indra's cleaner budget-driven tailwind above.

M:topic:1.reason: The structural emerging-market engine (about 60% of sales, 6-7% underlying once the India tax cut and Brazil destocking are stripped out) is real, but over 2027-28 it is outweighed by dated external headwinds on the base case: net material inflation of 1.3-1.8% of sales with Unilever the most exposed peer, developed-market competitors and private label pricing below what it needs, scanner volumes already (3.9)% in the US and (4.7)% in Western Europe, and a standing currency cost of about 2% of sales; consensus sales growth at the 32nd percentile fits, and sales hold only because price replaces volume. A slightly negative balance of real structural tailwinds against known, dated threats sits in the low 40s, coherent with the group's 38 but a little above it because the headwinds are of manageable size and the emerging-market leg is widening; just below Carlsberg's modest mature environment and above Entra's.

M:topic:2.reason: A broad, funded reset is largely delivered and visibly working: Ice Cream demerged, Foods agreed to McCormick for $15.7bn plus shares, brands cut from about 370 to 180, the €800m programme finished early with a new €1bn to 2029, about 90% of the executive team replaced with pay on growth, cash and ROIC, and 2026 brought the best volume in over a decade and two guidance raises. M:topic:1.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:1.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 42.0
M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: The external balance tilts slightly negative over two to three years: consolidation-friendly regulators, German value-over-volume pricing and African regulator-permitted price rises with M-Pesa's network effects are structural, but fibre overbuild against the German cable base (about 40% of underlying operating profit, about 95,000 broadband lines lost a quarter), the enacted ECJ ruling removing mid-contract price rises, a UK price fight under CMA caps to May 2028 and a 1 to 1.5 point annual translation drag leave European revenue flat to slightly down. Consensus sales growth at the 12th percentile is a fair read once translation and the Safaricom perimeter are allowed for; I sit just below Carlsberg's modest mature environment because the negative force is concentrated in the largest profit pool, and above Fevertree, coherent with the External change forces group's 43.

M:topic:2.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:2.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 68.0
M:topic:2.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:2.reason: A full reset largely delivered on time (Spain and Italy sold at good prices, the UK merged and the minority bought cheaply, net debt halved, 11,000 roles out against 10,000, a refreshed team and a cash-weighted incentive plan) now feeds dated earnings forces: GBP 1.0bn of UK synergies ahead of plan, a EUR 1.0bn net European cost programme and a cost-forcing 19.9% owner with a Tele2 record, held back by a gross-to-net conversion of perhaps two-thirds, an insider CEO with no successor, front-line fatigue, an H2 FY26 miss and a capital-light German response that cedes position. I sit above the Internal change forces group's 63 because whether the forces are already in consensus is scope (topic 7), not strength; it is a repair-led reset with outputs still lagging at EPS, so below NKT's working, growth-led change and level with Kitron's integration-plus-acquisition story.

M:topic:3.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:3.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 45.0
M:topic:3.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:3.reason: Concentrated, consolidating telecom markets with licence barriers, scale procurement and real moats in UK mobile, enterprise and African payments, against the disadvantaged position in German fixed (the largest pool, cable overbuilt by fibre, last on network quality), no European consumer pricing power, a single-customer wholesale line and a strong, cash-focused but deliberately unambitious management; groups average Industry 53, Advantage 42, Economic strength 30, Management 60. The financial profile is below the cost of capital (post-tax ROCE 5.5%; reported ROIC -0.3% at the 9th percentile is impairment-distorted, but new capital in Safaricom at 36% economics and a UK merger earning its cost of capital only by FY32 is not better), offset by an 18.4% free cash flow margin (86th percentile) and predictable guided lines, so it sits below Xvivo's one deep franchise and above Judges Scientific's warning-hit model.

M:topic:4.reason: An honest tracker for three years (FY24 and FY25 met, FY26 at the upper end on profit and cash, FY27 raised once at Q1) after a poor five-year record of two dividend cuts and a German TV-law miss at three times the estimate, with EBITDAaL missing consensus by 1 to 2% most years while cash beat. M:topic:5.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:5.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 48.0
M:topic:5.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:5.reason: The structure has strong gearing: a largely fixed cost base (1% of organic service revenue moves EBITDAaL 1.8% and EPS about 7%), financial leverage held at 2.3 to 2.4x that turns 1% of EBITDAaL into about 4% of EPS, large specific cost-out scope (EUR 1.0bn net, a possible doubling under Vega) and a capital loop that converts EBITDAaL growth into buybacks. It is held well short of 75 because pricing power is absent in both large European markets (ECJ, CMA caps), the gearing is running in reverse in the shrinking, wholly owned German pool while the growing loops (M-Pesa, Africa) are minority-shared, and refinancing drags 3 to 5% off EPS; the forecast EPS-to-revenue ratio of about four times is mostly buyback, and I sit above the Economic strength (30) and Financial forecasts (35) groups because they weigh returns and growth rather than the structure.

M:topic:2.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:2.reason: The heart programme is the largest product entry in the company's history: CE-marked in August, the FDA PMA filed in September on category-best data, a three-tier European rollout. Alongside it come the liver 510(k) pivot, tenfold disposable capacity, abdominal consolidation in Sweden and the 2025 cost programme, which together justify 20%-plus revenue growth. Netted against them are a services unit losing money for six quarters (-19% gross margin), a CFO seat empty for eight months, a record of slipped dates, FlowHawk stalling, and launch costs that absorb the growth and keep 2027 EPS flat. That is a little lower than the 68 Richard ruled too high, and a few points above the group's 59 because a launch of this size is a large force whether or not it has reached earnings yet; it sits between OEM International (66) and Odfjell Drilling (61).
